comments.content: Reordering fixes `invalid_credentials`, but the bug behind it is still here. The raw Supabase body contains `"error_code":...`, so `contains("code")` matches every auth error body. Any of those that also contains "invalid" and misses the specific checks above will still show "Invalid sync code". One example is the signup reply `{"error_code":"email_address_invalid","msg":"Email address \"x\" is invalid"}`, which does not contain the exact text "invalid email". Matching "sync code" or the RPC's own exception text would be tighter, or you could exclude bodies that contain `error_code`. Also, nothing in `app/src/test` covers `accountErrorResId`. A small test with the `invalid_credentials` body and a real sync-code error body would lock in the new order.

`AuthState.Loading` doesn't always clear on its own. In `AuthManager.observeSessionStatus`, the `NotAuthenticated` branch with `SessionRefreshResult.TRANSIENT_FAILURE` only logs "keeping current auth state", and that state is still the initial `Loading`. The `Authenticated` branch also blocks on `validateAuthenticatedSession` (a network call) before it sets `FullAccount`. So when the TV starts offline or on a slow network, the state can stay `Loading` well beyond 5 s, even with a valid session for the same account the file names.

In that case this code calls `signOut()`, which runs `clearAfterSignOut` and wipes the profiles and history. `signInWithEmail` then fails for the same network reason. The customer ends up signed out with their data deleted, on a box that was already signed in to their own account. The spec accepts that cost only for a *different* account (Decisions, AC-10).

There is a second problem: `signOut()` runs inside the processor's 20 s `withTimeoutOrNull`. Its network call uses up the sign-in budget, and a timeout can land in the middle of `clearAfterSignOut`, whose `runCatching` blocks swallow the cancellation and leave a partial wipe.

Suggestion: if the state is still `Loading` after the wait, don't wipe on a guess. Sign in directly, or compare against the email in the stored session (`auth.currentSessionOrNull()?.user?.email`). Only sign out when you know the account is different.

This only trims the ends of the email, but `loginFileAccountAction` strips every whitespace character before comparing. So `"a b@x.com"` counts as the same account as `"ab@x.com"`, yet the version with the space is what gets sent to the server. Use one normalisation for both, or compare only trimmed, lowercased emails.

This timeout can't cut off the network call, so the 20 s budget isn't enforced. `AuthManager.executeSupabaseJsonRequestAttempt` makes a blocking `client.newCall(request).execute()` call inside `withContext(Dispatchers.IO)`. Cancelling the coroutine doesn't interrupt that call, and `withTimeoutOrNull` can only return after the child block finishes. That block can include the 5 s settle wait, `signOut()` (another network call) and the primary request plus the fallback-origin retry, each limited only by OkHttp's connect/read timeouts. Together they can easily go past the phone's 30 s window, and then the result file shows up too late. Also, `signInWithEmail` catches `Exception`, which includes `CancellationException`, so a timed-out attempt is turned into an ordinary failure. Fix: make the HTTP call cancellable (`Call.cancel()` on cancellation via `suspendCancellableCoroutine`/`invokeOnCancellation`, or set an OkHttp `callTimeout`), or race the sign-in against a timer that writes the timeout result without waiting for the sign-in to finish.

`text` is built from `AuthHttpException.message`, which contains the whole server response body. A 5xx body that happens to include "timeout" (for example "upstream request timeout") will be reported as "could not reach the internet". Going the other way, `NoRouteToHostException` and `SSLException` aren't `ConnectException`s, so real connectivity failures fall through to the generic message. Match on exception types, plus the HTTP status for `AuthHttpException`, instead of substrings of the server body.

comments.content: A result file left over from an earlier attempt is never removed before the new sign-in starts. If KevBox Setup polls for `kevbox-login.result.json` and doesn't delete it itself first, it can read the old result straight away. Delete any existing result and `.tmp` file once the login file has been accepted.
